etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from French crédibilité, from Medieval Latin credibilitas, from Latin credibilis. By surface analysis, credible +‎ -ity.

definitions.definition: Reputation impacting one's ability to be believed.

quote.citation: 2022 January 26, “Network News: DfT awaits verdict on COVID 'partygate' scandal”, in RAIL, number 949, page 6:
quote.text: The 'partygate' controversy has played a major part in undermining the credibility of Boris Johnson and his Government and has led to calls from senior MPs for him to resign.

definitions.definition: (law) Believability of statements by a witness, as measured by whether the testimony is probable or improbable when judged by common experience.
